title: AI Tools Today
about: Where you meet AI every day, the kinds of tools, and their age rules.

cards.prompt: AI guesses from learned patterns. Does each one **use AI**, or follow **fixed steps** someone wrote?

items.label: A photo app finding pictures of your dog
A map predicting traffic on your way
Live captions on a video as people talk
Your keyboard suggesting the next word
A calculator adding up a bill

cards.hint: Does it guess from learned patterns, or follow the same steps every time?
cards.nudge: Could it ever be unsure? Guesses can be wrong; fixed steps give the same result.
cards.explanation: Finding your dog, traffic, captions and word suggestions are **guesses** from patterns: AI. A calculator and an alarm follow **fixed steps**. Many AI features are on by default, and many can be turned off.

cards.prompt: A **chat assistant** types replies, an **image generator** makes pictures, a **voice assistant** talks. Which suits each job?

pairs.left: Ideas for a birthday party, typed out
A picture of a dragon for a poster
A timer while your hands are floury
A menu in a language you can't read

cards.hint: What do you give the tool, and what do you need back?
cards.nudge: Floury hands can't type, and a menu you can't read needs its words changed.
cards.explanation: Typed ideas suit a **chat assistant**, pictures an **image generator**, hands-free a **voice assistant**, and a **translation app** changes the language. Many apps do several.

cards.prompt: Chat assistants include **ChatGPT** (OpenAI), **Claude** (Anthropic), **Copilot** (Microsoft) and **Gemini** (Google). Some also search the web or make pictures.

steps.text: Your friend says: "My AI app is the best. It's never wrong." What's the most accurate reply?

choices.text: "If it's the best, you don't need to check it"
choices.consequence: Even a very good model writes likely words, not checked facts. Any of them can be wrong.

choices.text: "Any chatbot can be wrong, so check what matters"
choices.consequence: Right: they're all language models, so any of them can hallucinate.

choices.text: "Use the newest version: it doesn't make mistakes"
choices.consequence: Newer models can be better, but they still pick likely words and still make mistakes.

cards.hint: How does every chat assistant write its answers, whoever made it?
cards.explanation: Every chat assistant is a language model picking likely words, so **any** of them can be wrong. Check the things that matter.

cards.title: Age rules and good habits
cards.body:
Every AI app has its own rules, including **who can use it**. Some say 18 or older; some allow 13 with a parent's OK. Rules differ by country, and they change.

- **Check the app's rules**, and **ask a parent or carer** before signing up.
- **Think twice before uploading photos** of you or friends.
- **Follow your school's AI rules.**

cards.prompt: A new AI app promises to turn your selfie into a cartoon.

steps.text: It asks for a selfie, a photo of a friend, and a tick for "I am 18 or older". You're 13. What do you do?

choices.text: Upload only your own selfie, leaving your friend out
choices.consequence: Leaving your friend out is good, but the app says 18 or older, and you're 13.

choices.text: Stop, and ask a parent or carer about the app
choices.consequence: Good: the app is for adults, and photos of you and a friend deserve a second thought.

choices.text: Ask your friend first, then upload both photos
choices.consequence: Asking your friend is good, but the app is for adults only, and ticking "18 or older" breaks its rules.

cards.hint: Look back at the age rules and good habits.
cards.explanation: The app says 18+, so it isn't for you yet, even with only your own photo or your friend's OK. **Stop and ask a parent or carer.**

cards.prompt: For schoolwork, is each use of an AI tool **usually fine**, or one to **check with your teacher first**?

items.label: Explaining a topic you're stuck on
Spotting spelling mistakes in your notes
Making a picture for an art task

cards.hint: Does the AI help you learn, or make part of what you hand in?
cards.nudge: Does the AI make something that ends up in what you hand in?
cards.explanation: Help that lets you **learn** is usually fine. If AI **makes part of what you hand in** (writing, art, translating a language task), check with your teacher first.

cards.prompt: Is each one true of **every** AI chat assistant, or only **some** of them (or none)?

items.label: Writes its reply one word at a time

cards.hint: What do all share because of how they're built, and what extras do some add?
cards.nudge: Which come from being a language model, and which are extras (or impossible)?
cards.explanation: Every chat assistant **learned from text**, writes **a word at a time** and **can be wrong**. Searching, pictures and today's news are **extras** only some have, and none is never wrong.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- Every chat assistant writes likely words, so any can be wrong.
- AI is also inside everyday apps: maps, photos, keyboards.
- Check each app's age rules, and ask a parent or carer.

Next: the module quiz.
